# The core rules

Every core rule lives in `src/domain`: pure functions, with no database, screen or network code. The app, the import, the reviews and the AI assistant all call the same ones. Read them in this order; each builds on the ones before.

| Rule | What it decides |
|---|---|
| [Weeks and plans](weeks-and-plans.md) | Which week it is, and what a goal’s plan says its number should be in any week. |
| [A goal’s status](status.md) | What the numbers say (the calculated status), and the official status everyone sees: the owner’s call, unless it has gone stale. |
| [The projection](projection.md) | Where a number lands by its due week if the recent trend holds: the likeliest value and a range around it. |
| [What a check-in must say](check-in.md) | What a check-in needs before it can be posted, and the record it becomes. |
| [Numbers and names](numbers-and-names.md) | How a typed number is kept and shown, which numbers are questioned, and how two goals or two people with the same name are told apart. |
| [Flags, the trend and needs attention](flags.md) | Why a goal is flagged, which way it is heading, and whether it needs attention or is being handled. |
| [The scorecard](scorecard.md) | The cells at the top of a goal’s page: against plan, since last week, what’s left, and how likely it is to hit the target. |
| [The change engine](change-engine.md) | The one way many changes come in at once: a spreadsheet, set-up, the bulk check-in grid, the data tables and MCP. |
| [The field table](field-table.md) | For every column a person fills in: whether a new row must have it, its format, an example and what an empty cell does, said once for the template, the workbook’s Start here sheet, Help and the import. |
| [Kinds, levels and near misses](import-levels.md) | Every problem the change engine finds is data: a kind, and a level its kind fixes (Must fix, Check, or said); problems group by kind, one answer covers a group, and a name one letter out is asked about, never guessed. |
| [What an import read, and leaving rows out](import-preview.md) | Before an import is saved, it says which sheets and columns it read and which it did not, counts by sheet, and may leave named rows out with the rows that depend on them; worked-out cells a file edited are counted and said, never read. |
| [The header row, and headers that are nearly right](import-header.md) | A sheet’s header row is found in its first ten rows; a column under another name the field table gives it is read as that column, and one a letter out is asked about once, at every door. |
| [Undoing an import, and past imports](import-undo.md) | Every import, bulk edit and change through MCP is one entry in the change log that can be undone as a whole by whoever made it or an admin; Undo says first which rows changed since and will stay, and why. |
| [Deciding in a review](review-decide.md) | A goal behind leaves a review with a next step (an owner and a week) or an accepted risk with a reason; the next session opens with what the last one agreed. |
| [A year’s end](year-end.md) | A cycle’s real first and last days, where it stands on a day, and the week its results are judged at: the clock, not a button, ends a year. |
| [Starting the next year](start-next-year.md) | Which cycle everyone is in, what an admin’s start prepares and reads back first, and when it can be undone. |
| [Levels](levels.md) | Which levels a goal can have, what each is called, which is the everyday one, and how they sort: read from one place. |
| [The carry rule, and what comes with a goal](carry.md) | How a goal that carries on is set up in the next year, what comes with it, and how its copy stays true until someone uses it. |
| [The workspace: cycles, teams, names, leaving and what needs attention](workspace.md) | What Workspace says about each cycle and team, the longest name a workspace may have, who may leave, and what its overview lists as needing attention. |
| [The directory: who People lists, what a search finds, and where old addresses lead](directory.md) | People’s order and search, a page at a time; the line beside a person; a team’s people and goals by status; and where People’s and Teams’ old Workspace addresses now lead. |
| [Day one: set-up’s steps and “Getting started”](day-one.md) | How many steps set-up counts for the path chosen, and what Home’s “Getting started” tells each person in a workspace’s first weeks. |
| [The goal map](map.md) | The critical path, what the map shows when folded, what a parent says about the goals under it, which trees are in trouble, and finding a goal by name or key. |
| [Acting on a goal: its buttons, and next steps and asks](goal-act.md) | Which main button a goal’s page offers whoever is looking, the plain button beside it, and the one list of everything asked and agreed on the goal, each row with at most one button. |
| [A goal’s history](goal-history.md) | Every week of a goal, checked in or not, its comments, what reviews said and its changes, under four filters with counts. |
| [Who a comment reaches](comment-reach.md) | The line under a goal’s comment box: everyone in the workspace can read a comment, and the goal’s owner and the people watching it see it on Home. |
| [Goal entry](goal-entry.md) | What a goal needs, what can’t be saved and who may save it: one rule for New goal, the edit page, set-up’s cards, a spreadsheet’s Goals rows and the AI tools, in the same words. |
| [Years and weeks](years-and-weeks.md) | A goal’s weeks are counted from its cycle’s start and shown as a goal year’s week with its dates and their year; one rule converts each way, for the picker, the sheet and the AI tools. |
| [New goal](new-goal.md) | New goal asks what, then who and where, then how it’s measured, then reads it back; its level starts from the goal it feeds, and “Feeds into” suggests the goals one level up. |
| [The read-back](read-back.md) | New goal’s last step reads the goal back in sentences, with what was left as usual and what you said, then says what happens after it is published: when the first check-in is due, who sees it, the reviews it joins and how long it can be taken back. |
| [Proposed goals](proposed.md) | A goal can be proposed before anyone is held to it: visible to everyone, never judged, nothing due, counted apart, and made active by one deliberate act of its owner or an admin. |
| [A goal not born late](not-born-late.md) | A stage already past when a goal is set up is asked about, and one said to be done counts as on time; a goal’s first number may restart its plan. |
| [Finding things](finding.md) | What a search matches, the near miss offered when nothing does, and the one search per kind of thing (goals, people, teams) that every list, picker and Find calls. |
| [Navigation: the menu, the lit item and a page’s name](navigation.md) | Which places the menu lists for a viewer, where a module’s items go, which one is lit at an address, what a page is called, and what a Back link says. |
| [The Goals page: whose goals, how they are grouped, and the switch](goals-page.md) | Which scope tabs someone has and which opens, each scope’s own grouping, what the Needs attention switch counts, the line that counts the goals shown, and how old addresses and saved views open. |
| [Home: what is asked of you today](home.md) | Whether Home leads with one thing asked of the viewer today, and its one primary action, or says in one quiet line that nothing is. |

## The numbers the rules turn on

From `src/domain/thresholds.ts`:

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RULES.onTrack` | 0.95 | Share of the planned change for on track |
| `RULES.atRisk` | 0.8 | Share of the planned change for at risk (below it is off track) |
| `RULES.wellAhead` | 1.2 | Share of the planned change for well ahead (still on track; asks why) |
| `RULES.staleDays` | 14 | Days without a check-in before a goal has no recent update |
| `RULES.lateWeeksOff` | 2 | Weeks late beyond which a stage is off track |
| `TREND_SPAN` | 3 | Check-ins the trend looks back over |
